name: Kundl
kurzbeschreibung: A residential and industrial town in the Unterinntal valley, home to Schloss and the baroque parish church St. Nikolaus.
beschreibung:
Overview

Kundl is a historic market town in the Tyrolean Unterinntal in the Kufstein district, situated at an altitude of 526 metres south of the Inn River. Home to around 4,900 residents, the municipality is located at the mouth of the wild Kundler Klamm gorge, which cuts through limestone cliffs towards the high valley of Wildschönau. Kundl represents a fascinating harmony of natural wonders, historic sacred architecture, and major industrial significance. Alongside world-renowned manufacturing enterprises such as Lindner Tractors and Sandoz Pharmaceuticals, the town preserves living craftsmanship, housing Tyrol's only stone-turning workshop and the late-Gothic pilgrimage church of St. Leonhard on the Meadow.

History

Settlement in Kundl extends back into pre-Roman antiquity, highlighted by major Hallstatt and La Tène iron-age burial excavations. The town was first documented in 788 as Chundilao in the records of the Diocese of Salzburg. For centuries, inhabitants lived from agriculture, logging, and cutting unique river stone in the gorge. A spiritual landmark was achieved in 1481 with the completion of the pilgrimage church of St. Leonhard on the Meadow by master Christian Nickinger, traditionally consecrated in 1512 by Emperor Maximilian I. In the 20th century, Kundl emerged as an industrial powerhouse: Hermann Lindner began tractor production here in 1946, while the local brewery was converted in 1946 into a groundbreaking penicillin manufacturing site that grew into Sandoz.

Getting There

Kundl benefits from premier transport accessibility. Motorists arrive via the A12 Inntal Autobahn using the Wörgl-West or Kramsach exits and continue along the B171 federal highway directly into town. Kundl railway station on the Lower Inn Valley main line is served at frequent intervals by Tyrolean S-Bahn suburban trains (line S4) and regional trains, offering fast direct connections to Innsbruck, Jenbach, Wörgl, and Kufstein. Regional buses link the railway station and the village centre directly to trailheads and neighbouring valleys.

Tips

The premier natural attraction is walking through the Kundler Klamm gorge: the 3.5-kilometre barrier-free, family-friendly trail winds alongside turbulent whitewaters beneath soaring 200-metre rock faces. At the gorge entrance, the Sandbichler Stone Turning workshop demonstrates the unique craft of shaping river pebbles into decorative polished bowls. Culture enthusiasts must visit the pilgrimage church of St. Leonhard on the Meadow to admire its shingled facade, carved stone portals, and gothic treasures. During summer, the charming Wildschönau vintage tractor-train runs from the upper end of the gorge to Mühltal.
